prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a target protein together so that the ubiquitin-proteasome system eliminates it, from heterobifunctional degraders to the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues.

statement.case_for: After the first round I keep targeted protein degradation as a single-part prize, but I now state more clearly why it is one achievement. The unifying principle is induced proximity: a small molecule creates a ternary complex that redirects the ubiquitin-proteasome system, whether the molecule is bifunctional (Crews and Deshaies, who conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept) or monovalent (the thalidomide-class glues, whose mechanism rests on Handa's identification of cereblon as the target). The mechanistic evidence is in physical terms that I value: structurally characterised ternary complexes, cooperativity, and degradation kinetics, all reproduced widely and independent of clinical outcome. B054 also remains the ballot most often named across the files (two preferences and five alternatives), the only one where members reach the same area from different directions, and it keeps the configuration to three people.
statement.case_against: Credit is still the weak point. Ciulli (structure-guided VHL ligands), Sakamoto (first PROTAC), Ito (co-identification of cereblon), Gray and Kim are left out, and any three-person cut will be contestable. If the committee judges the heterobifunctional and glue strands to be two discoveries, my single citation would be too broad and Chabes's narrower Crews and Deshaies part is the better-defined unit. No heterobifunctional degrader is approved, so those who weigh clinical maturity heavily have a legitimate objection. Finally, the round-1 exchange did not remove the dispersion over seven ballots, and I cannot claim that B054 is close to five votes.

responses.point: Chabes proposes Crews and Deshaies only for heterobifunctional degraders, as the second part of a two-part prize with Liu's base editing, and notes that Handa, Ito and Ciulli are omitted.
responses.response: I have not changed my view that the glue mechanism belongs in the citation, but your narrower version is the fallback I would accept if the committee decides the strands are separate. My reservation about the two-part pairing is practical: Liu plus Crews and Deshaies is three people, but it leaves no room for Komor and Gaudelli, whom you yourself name as a cost, and it puts two chemical-biology tools in one prize without a unifying statement. I would rather have one well-attributed degradation prize than a pairing whose second part depends on resolving the CRISPR overlap. If the committee prefers a two-part prize I would support it only with B054 as the lead part.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, asks whether B054 should rest on the PROTAC concept, the cereblon mechanism or both, whether the absence of an approved PROTAC delays recognition, and prefers perovskites (Miyasaka, Snaith, Park).
responses.response: My answer to your question is both, because the scientific claim is the redirection of the ubiquitin-proteasome system by a small molecule, and approval status does not change that. Cereblon-based glues already have approved drugs, so the principle is clinically validated even though no heterobifunctional degrader is. On B017, I accept that the absorber discovery and the efficiency rise are well demonstrated, but my concern about attribution stands: Park versus Grätzel, Kanatzidis or Seok is as open as my own Handa versus Ciulli question, and stability bears on maturity. I have therefore moved B017 into my alternatives, since it is the only other ballot with an identical trio proposed by two members, but I do not prefer it over B054.

responses.point: Åqvist lists B054 as an alternative and prefers first-principles molecular dynamics (Car and Parrinello) for its clean two-person attribution and decades of validation.
responses.response: I agree that attribution for Car and Parrinello is the cleanest on the list, and as someone who values mechanism stated in physical terms I respect the method. My difficulty is the one you raise yourself: the 1998 DFT prize and the machine-learned potential lineage make the distinct, separable discovery harder to state, and only two members ranked it highly. Since you placed B054 among your alternatives, I would ask whether you could support a degradation citation that names Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and whether you would still prefer Ciulli over Handa for the third place. My reasoning remains that Handa's identification of cereblon explains the mechanism of thalidomide, while Ciulli's work, though important, is an optimisation of the concept.

responses.point: Somfai pairs C-N coupling (Buchwald and Hartwig) with base editing (Liu) and reports that only he ranked B065 in the opening ballots.
responses.response: The ligand-design story for C-N coupling is a model of mechanistic chemistry and I do not dispute its adoption. The difficulty is that it has had no support from other members and follows the 2010 cross-coupling prize, so the committee would be asked to decide the question of novelty without a second advocate. On base editing, I take your point that the chemical novelty is thinner than for synthetic methods, which is the same concern about the 2020 CRISPR prize that I raised in round 1, and it reinforces my keeping B069 only as an alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards PROTACs and cereblon glues as one achievement or two, and whether Handa, Ciulli or Sakamoto is the right third name beside Crews and Deshaies.
Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader will lead several members to prefer a prize that is clinically more mature, such as B069 or B017.
Whether B054 can reach five votes given that the first round showed only two explicit preferences for it and no ballot with more than two.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need for any shortlisted candidate. My own field (respiratory enzymes, electron and proton transfer) is closest to B043 and B062, neither of which is in my preferred configuration now, so my interest in them does not affect my position. I remain a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which is not relevant to any shortlisted candidate.
